title: Coefficient preparation at the approximation radius of an immediate prime extension
statement:
Let $K\subseteq L$ be complete fields [def-weil-field] with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values. Set $F^\circ=\{x\in F:|x|\le1\}$ [def-trf-valuation-ring], $\widetilde F=F^\circ/\{x:|x|<1\}$ and $\Gamma_F=|F^\times|$ for $F=K,L$. Suppose $p=\operatorname{char}\widetilde K>0$, $[L:K]=p$, $\widetilde L=\widetilde K$ and $\Gamma_L=\Gamma_K$. Here degree means vector-space dimension. There exist $\theta\in L\setminus K$, numbers $0<r<R=|\theta|$, and coefficients $b,a_1,\ldots,a_{p-1}\in K$ such that $L=K(\theta)$ and its monic minimal polynomial (the monic polynomial of least degree vanishing at $\theta$) in $K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] is
$$f(T)=T^p+\sum_{i=1}^{p-1}a_iT^i+b.$$
They satisfy
$$r=\inf_{c\in K}|\theta-c|<|\theta-c|\quad(c\in K),\qquad |f(c)|=|\theta-c|^p\quad(c\in K),$$
$$|b|=R^p,\qquad |p|R^p<r^p,\qquad |a_i|R^i<r^p\quad(2\le i<p),\qquad |a_1|\le r^{p-1}.$$
If $|a_1|<r^{p-1}$, the choices also satisfy $|a_1|R<r^p$. The integer $p$ in an absolute value denotes its image in the field; in characteristic $p$ it is zero. The sum over $2\le i<p$ is empty when $p=2$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4, proof of (i) for immediate extensions, printed pp. 39--40: translation and shrinking before discarding the higher coefficients; the inseparable case is the preceding paragraph. The evaluation identity follows from uniqueness of the extending absolute value applied to the conjugates of the minimal polynomial.

mathlib_searches.query: An immediate extension of prime degree over a complete nonarchimedean field admits a minimal polynomial with small higher coefficients and linear coefficient bounded by the distance to the base field
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: spectralNorm_eq_norm_coeff_zero_rpow gives only a constant-coefficient identity, and IsPurelyInseparable.minpoly_eq gives only the inseparable case. Neither provides the translated higher-coefficient and linear-coefficient bounds at the nonattained approximation radius.
